chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If something flows from your manhood, either pre-seminal fluid (madhi) or semen (mani), and you are in the prayer, do not wash it, do not break the prayer, and do not invalidate the ablution for it. And if it reaches your behind, that is merely like phlegm. And everything that comes out from you after the ablution is from the sexual veins or from the haemorrhoids, and it is not significant, so do not wash it from your clothes unless it dirties you.

key_terms.النُّخَامَةِ: Phlegm, used here as a simile for minor, non-significant discharge
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: Ablution, the ritual washing before prayer
key_terms.مَذْيٍ: Pre-seminal fluid, a thin clear fluid discharged during arousal
key_terms.وَدْيٍ: Semen or seminal fluid, often used interchangeably with madhi in this context

ai.seo_question: Does pre-seminal fluid or semen invalidate wudu or break the prayer if it occurs during salat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of minor seminal discharge (madhi) during prayer, establishing that it does not invalidate wudu or require breaking the salah, treating it as a negligible impurity similar to phlegm. Shia scholars emphasize the distinction between this minor fluid and major semen (mani), noting that post-wudu emissions are often attributed to natural bodily conditions like veins or hemorrhoids, thus preserving the continuity of worship. The ruling underscores the principle of ease in ritual purity, requiring washing only if the fluid causes noticeable dirtiness (ithqar) rather than mere presence.
